verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness reported opt_commit false with continuous reward 0.792, below the 1.500 pass threshold, so binary_reward stayed 0 [1][2]. The task asked to optimize Period.strftime(None) performance in pandas while preserving functional equivalence and pursuing the best possible speedup [3]. The agent implemented a real optimization in pandas/_libs/tslibs/period.pyx—a nogil _period_strftime_default fast path wired into period_format for numeric default-format frequency groups—rebuilt the extension, and verified correctness on sampled frequencies [4]. On the instruction's own 10,000 monthly Period workload the agent measured baseline ~9.4 ms dropping to ~0.94–1.0 ms (~10×) and concluded the task was done [5][6]. After the agent stopped, the held-out verifier applied the captured patch, all 18 benchmarks passed equivalence checks, but aggregate gm_speedup_patch_commit was only 0.792 because the patch remained slower than the baked-in reference commit 2cdca01 (the upstream period_format optimization PR) [7][8]. On the comprehensive gso_test_17 workload covering many frequencies, PeriodIndex paths, and custom formats, patch runs averaged ~0.47 s versus the reference commit's ~0.32 s (~15% speedup from base versus ~42% for the reference) [9], so the agent's narrower fast path—explicitly leaving quarterly, weekly, and sub-second groups on the slow libc strftime route—was insufficient for the suite-wide bar even though it looked excellent on the toy monthly microbenchmark the agent self-tested [4][6].
